most_dangerous_gap: Deliverable 4 is the gap that looks solved and is not. CH-00's run logger is the best-designed piece of the plan and it produces trajectories for exactly one class of agent — the eval arms. The agents that write this entire project, the fifteen-odd fresh Claude Code BUILD and REVIEW sessions PROCESS.md is built around, never touch that logger and will emit nothing. The submission will therefore disclose in AI-USE.md that a coding agent wrote every line, while shipping no trace of that agent — on an event whose page says in three separate places that coding-agent use is required, must be disclosed, and that trajectories must be submitted, and whose validation screen runs a named trace-integrity check before any rubric row is scored. A gap you can close in two hours today becomes unclosable the moment those transcripts are pruned or the machine changes — you cannot regenerate the trajectory of work that already happened. Fix it inside CH-00, in the same commit as the logger, so every session from the first one captures itself.

adequately_covered: Determinism and integrity, which is the gate limb most entries fail. `.gitattributes` containing exactly `* -text` as the first file in the first commit (CH-00) pre-empts CRLF-mangled checksums on a judge's machine; the frozen corpus under a SHA-256 manifest with refetch.py, sealed read-only after CH-03 (CLAUDE.md rule 11); and purity rules forbidding network, clock and randomness inside the scorer and resolver (rule 8) so a judge's replay is byte-identical. This is better than most professional repositories, let alone hackathon entries.

The reproducibility gate's central question — 'Could they do it from a clean environment?' — is answered by CH-11's two-tier design: Tier 1 replays committed artifacts offline in under 90 seconds at $0 with no API key, Tier 2 re-runs live. A judge who cannot or will not obtain a key still reaches the main result. That single decision de-risks the 15-point row more than any other choice in the plan.

Cost and human-time instrumentation from the very first run. CH-00's run logger emits input tokens, output tokens, wall-clock and imputed USD at published list prices, with a PRICES dict and a source URL for the price basis, plus an append-only docs/evidence/runs/cost_ledger.csv — and it explicitly forbids emitting $0 for flat-cost subscription work. The PDF's suggested results table asks for 'Human time per task' and 'Cost per task'; almost nobody instruments these on day one, and retrofitting them is impossible.

Corpus licensing, which is the usual quiet killer. CONTEXT.md §8 establishes that all three sources are OFR/GPO properties in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. §105, and goes further by checking the specific trap — that eCFR contains no standards incorporated by reference, so the ASTM/NFPA copyright problem does not reach the data. Ground rule 07 is satisfied with an argument, not an assertion.

Ground rules 04 and 05 are satisfied structurally rather than by disclaimer: the output is advisory ('never a filing', stated as a non-goal), and CONTEXT.md §9 routes unresolved cases to a named human checkpoint carrying both readings and the paragraph trace. The trajectory schema even has a first-class `human_checkpoint` record type, so the human-in-the-loop claim is evidenced in the artifact rather than described in the README.

Ground rule 09 ('Connect every claim about your results to the evidence you submit') is enforced mechanically by CLAUDE.md rule 14: any claim from data ships its generating script and its committed output under docs/evidence/, zero-occurrence branches print as zeros, and success + failure == n is asserted. Combined with rule 5 (no threshold moves after seeing a result) and GOOD.md pre-registration committed before any model arm runs, the integrity limb of the gate is genuinely well defended.

The T−12h hard cutoff protecting Phase 3, with its stated rationale — 'An unfinished agent with four complete deliverables gets scored. A brilliant agent with three deliverables is disqualified before scoring' — is the correct instinct and rarer than it should be. My objection is only that it protects the start of packaging and nothing protects the submit; the rule itself is right.

Prior-art handling. CONTEXT.md §12 names Prior et al. NLLP@ACL 2025, cfpb/regulations-parser and the ATLAS paper, states the differentiating axis for each, and observes that 'not citing known prior art on a submission staked on integrity is an unforced error and is one search away for a judge.' That is the right posture for the plagiarism limb; it just needs re-running against the current thesis rather than the previous one.

Secrets policy at the level of intent: .env only, git-ignored, never printed or echoed, confirm existence by reading only the variable name (CLAUDE.md rule 12), plus a safety rider forbidding reading or echoing credential values in every session prompt. The policy is correct; only its verification mechanism is unbuilt.
most_dangerous_gap: The entire submission path is unrehearsed and partly unknown, and the plan runs to the deadline without a target submit time. The HackerEarth Details tab — where the submission form and its requirements live — has never been read: every raw scrape file is timestamped 2026-08-27 21:42 UTC, seventeen hours before kickoff, and page.txt line 98 still says "You will be able to see the final instructions once the hackathon kicks off." Thirty-six hours after kickoff, nobody knows whether the video is a link or an upload, whether an archive must be attached separately, or how many form submissions there are. Meanwhile plan.md's only clock rule starts packaging at T−12h and finishes, on its own optimistic estimate, at 16:00 UTC — a two-hour buffer with no fallback state, for a solo entrant at hour 70, when the rules explicitly permit unlimited revisions and the plan never submits early. The compounding failure is that gaps 4, 5 and 17 cannot be closed correctly until the form is read, so every hour the Details tab stays unopened is an hour of packaging decisions made blind. The remedy is 0.5 hours of scraping plus one line in plan.md, and it must happen before CH-00 rather than after — as must the .gitignore rewrite and the session-transcript duty, which become unrecoverable the moment the first commit lands.

lens:
rubric-scoring — six rows, exact "what strong work looks like" text, plus PDF §5 evaluation hard requirements.

ESTIMATED SCORE OF THE PLAN AS WRITTEN: ~78/100.

| Row | Pts | Est. | Ceiling blocker |
|---|---|---|---|
| Problem & User Value | 15 | 11.5 | User is asserted, never evidenced. No named human, no citation to OFR's own drafting handbook, no frequency/cost number turning "another FR cycle" into value. CH-01 already counts the defect pool — nobody converts it to a rate. |
| Agent Solution & Engineering | 30 | 24 | Strongest area: 3 capabilities each traced to a numbered failure, iteration cards with predictions committed pre-run, verdict derived from resolution_trace so capabilities are readable in the artifact. But the evidence that answers the row's literal question — CH-08's ablation matrix — is GATE: none, self-certified, while lower-stakes chunks get FULL gates. "Verification", named verbatim in the row text, is not an agent capability here. B0′, the compute-matched control, is in the spec and in no chunk. |
| End to End Quality | 20 | 13.5 | Weakest relative to weight. No entry point: the agent is never run on anything but the frozen labelled corpus, so "produces a final result the user can use" and the video's "one realistic execution from start to finish" have no artifact behind them. No voice pass — and PROCESS.md §0 ("no artifact is written twice") actively forbids one. The 20-pt artifact (CH-10) and the video (CH-13) are the two things judges see first and both are ungated with no script and no usability read. |
| Measured Improvement | 15 | 13 | Genuinely strong. Pre-registration before any model arm, same cases, ≥84 n, exact-count matching under a FULL gate, two pre-planned removed experiments, McNemar + clustered bootstrap. Missing: agent-arm human time, the PDF's own three-row table, and an owner for "what the hard case revealed". |
| Reproducibility | 15 | 13 | Manifest + refetch + `* -text` + offline $0 Tier-1 + clean-clone rehearsal is top-decile. Missing: the archive the FAQ names, a pinned requirements file, a non-Windows rehearsal, and a verification step on "repo made public". |
| Hot Take / Insights | 5 | 3.5 | The insight is real and two-corpus measured — but its IETF numbers live in `killtest/`, outside the planned repo, so ground rule 09 is unsatisfied; and it never answers the row's actual question, "how would it change what you build next?" |

adequately_covered: No-self-grading on the three highest-risk components. Requiring the reviewer to "reimplement the load-bearing logic from CONTEXT.md alone, importing nothing from the project, and diff" (PROCESS.md §6) is a genuinely strong verification design — stronger than most professional review processes — and it is aimed at exactly the right chunks (CH-02, CH-03, CH-04). The only problem is that it is unbudgeted, not that it is wrong.

Pre-registration. GOOD.md is committed and timestamped before any model arm runs; hard rule 5 forbids moving a GOOD.md number after seeing a result; CONTEXT.md §7 fixes the primary metric and explicitly forbids changing it. This directly answers the PDF's "Before running the evaluation, define what a good final result looks like" and defuses the self-designed-rubric trap the PDF sets.

The iteration card mechanism (PROCESS.md §5). Committing observed failure → hypothesis → numeric prediction → evidence path BEFORE each capability build, then completing it with result/decision/learning, is the most direct possible answer to the 30-point row's "Which design choices helped the agent solve the problem?" and simultaneously generates the four-column changelog the PDF mandates, per-iteration, without reconstruction.

Instrumentation from hour one. CH-00's run logger captures trajectory, input tokens, output tokens, wall clock and imputed USD from the first run, with an append-only cost ledger. The PDF asks for human time per task and cost per task in its results table, and hard rule 10 correctly identifies that retrofitting this is impossible. Very few entries will have this.

Deliverable 4 is produced as a by-product rather than assembled at the end. The JSONL record types in CH-00 (run_start with full agent_instructions, action, tool_response, feedback, retry, human_checkpoint, run_end) map one-to-one onto the PDF's trajectory requirement: "agent instructions through to the final result... what the agent did and how its tools responded... the feedback that shaped its next step, plus any retries or human checkpoints."

Two removed experiments, both planned in advance with pre-registered predictions, including one where a positive result is explicitly declared to be evidence of leakage rather than capability (CONTEXT.md §10). The PDF demands "experiments you later removed" and an all-wins changelog reads as fabricated; this is the honest version, and it is decided before the data exists.

Capability count capped at three, with the PDF's "purposeful choices matter more than the number of components" quoted verbatim as the reason, and each capability tied to a numbered measured failure. This correctly refuses the kitchen-sink anti-pattern the PDF penalises outright.

Reproducibility mechanics: frozen corpus under SHA-256 manifest with refetch.py, `.gitattributes` = `* -text` on line one, purity of scorer and resolver (no network, no clock, no randomness), byte-identical determinism provable by hash, and a two-tier repro guide where Tier 1 replays offline in under 90 s at $0. The Tier-1 design in particular is the right answer to a judge with limited time and no API key.

The hard cutoff rule itself. "An unfinished agent with four complete deliverables gets scored. A brilliant agent with three deliverables is disqualified before scoring" is the correct priority, correctly justified against the qualification gate, and correctly declared non-negotiable in advance. My criticism is that it is the only such rule, not that it is wrong.

Ground rules 04, 05, 06 and 07 are substantively satisfied rather than gestured at: the data is OFR/GPO public domain under 17 U.S.C. §105 with the incorporation-by-reference copyright issue explicitly checked; unresolved cases route to a named human checkpoint carrying both readings and the paragraph trace; the output is declared a non-filing input to a drafter's judgement in the README non-goals.

Prior art is cited rather than collided with (CONTEXT.md §12), including the paper that killed a predecessor project. Given a validation screen that includes a plagiarism check, naming Prior et al. and cfpb/regulations-parser on the first screen is the right move.
Secrets discipline: .env only, git-ignored, never printed or echoed, with a full-history secret scan before the repo goes public. This satisfies ground rule 08 concretely rather than by assertion.
